messages:
Daniel Park: Heads up — team dinner in Tokyo on company card. Total JPY 14,200. Two teammates paid me back in cash (JPY 4,200 each) but I only have a single restaurant receipt showing JPY 14,200. Can I submit the full charge and note the reimbursements, or do I need separate receipts?

Hannah (People Ops): You can submit the company card charge for the business portion. Attach the restaurant receipt and include a short note explaining the cash reimbursements and amounts. Accounting prefers either: (a) cash reimbursements returned into the company card (recorded) or (b) teammate receipts if they paid on card.

Daniel Park: Teammates paid me cash at the table. They didn't keep separate receipts. Is that ok?

Priya (Manager): I confirm this was a team client dinner and approve the business portion. Approving Daniel's note that two teammates reimbursed him JPY 4,200 each.

Claire (Accounting): OK. Process will be: submit the hotel/meal expense with the JPY 14,200 receipt, add notes: "2 teammates reimbursed cash JPY 4,200 each, manager approved Priya". Accounting will deduct the personal portion if any. If you want a cleaner record, deposit the cash reimbursements to the company card or to Finance and attach the bank slip.

Expense Bot: Reminder: attach original itemized receipt (photo/pdf). If you deposit cash reimbursements, attach the deposit slip or an itemized note. Use category "meals" and set currency JPY.

Daniel Park: Got it. I'll submit the 14,200 receipt, note the cash reimbursements and Priya's approval. Will ask teammates to either give me a small written note or I'll drop the cash to Finance next week. Thanks.
